resources.string: OmoAuto shows Android Auto on your motorcycle\'s display. Finish these steps once.
Developer mode stays on. After a phone restart, or a Force stop of Android Auto, the head unit server stops: only step 3 is needed again (⋮ › Start head unit server).
All set. This screen returns if a step stops passing.
Android Auto from Google Play is required. OmoAuto connects to it on this phone.
Tap Open Android Auto settings below.
Scroll all the way down to Version (for example “Version 17.9…”) and tap it about 10 times in a row.
When “Allow development settings?” appears, tap OK. Developer mode is now on. Come back here and tap Done.
Tap Open Android Auto settings below.
Tap ⋮ at the top right and choose Start head unit server.
The ⋮ menu has no Start head unit server? Developer mode is not on yet. Do step 2 first (tap Version about 10 times), then open ⋮ again.
Couldn\'t check the head unit server.

Android Auto only connects to a head unit that presents a certificate. Get keys downloads the free sample certificate and key from Open Headunit, an open-source head unit project on GitHub, checks their fingerprints and keeps them inside the app only.

They are published openly for testing, so everyone gets the same two files. They aren\'t secret, contain nothing about you, your phone or your motorcycle, and don\'t unlock anything. The certificate is labelled “Google-Android-Reference”, the name of that sample identity. OmoAuto downloads them from the exact version it was tested with.
GitHub sent different files than OmoAuto expects, so they weren\'t used. Try again later, or import files.
Download failed (%1$s). Check your internet connection.
That file has no certificate or private key.
The certificate isn\'t valid yet. Check the phone\'s date.
The private key is password-protected. Export it without a password.
Unsupported key type. Use an RSA or EC key in PKCS#8 format.
The private key couldn\'t be read.
The private key doesn\'t belong to this certificate.
On Android 12 and older, phones only find Wi-Fi Direct devices such as your motorcycle while Location is on. OmoAuto does not read or store your location.
Location is off, so your motorcycle cannot be found.
%1$s phones can stop Android Auto in the background, so it cannot answer OmoAuto. Let it keep running:
Come back here and tap Done.
Tap Open Autostart settings and turn on Android Auto.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery saver, and choose No restrictions.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery, and choose Unrestricted.
In Settings, Battery, Background usage limits, make sure Android Auto is not in Sleeping apps or Deep sleeping apps.
Tap Open Autostart settings and allow Android Auto to auto-launch.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery usage, and turn on Allow background activity.
Tap Open Autostart settings and allow Android Auto to start in the background.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery, and allow high background power usage.
Tap Open Autostart settings, find Android Auto, turn off Manage automatically, and turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery, and allow it to run in the background.
Tap Open Autostart settings (Phone Master) and allow Android Auto.
Tap Open Android Auto app info, then Battery, and choose No restrictions.
Tap Open Android Auto app info.
Come back to OmoAuto. This step turns green by itself.
